$schema.purpose: Accepted reads of a member assigned in initAsync() that go through neither readiness discipline. Enforced by ai/scripts/lint/lint-deferred-member-readiness.mjs.
$schema.key: <relPath>#<method>:<member> — one obligation per method+member, NOT per read. Keyed by symbol rather than line so an unrelated edit above the site does not force a re-baseline, which is exactly where a real regression slips through. A private method appears as `##name`.
$schema.shape: How the read fails the invariant: bare-read (TypeError during the window) | truthy-skip (work silently skipped, caller told nothing) | optional-chain (evaluates undefined and flows on). Drift in shape fails the lint: a truthy-skip becoming a bare-read turns silence into a crash, and the old reason no longer describes it.
$schema.reason: REQUIRED. Entries fall in two honest classes — 'deliberate' (examined, the behaviour is intended) and 'pre-existing, un-audited' (recorded at introduction so the gate works from day one; assessing it is a separate lane per #16644's Out of Scope). Inventing a confident rationale for a site nobody examined would make this a suppression list wearing a reason field.
$schema.witness: REQUIRED, and its paths are resolved by the lint. A witness naming a file deleted two refactors ago reads exactly like one naming a live file.
$schema.baselineHistory: First proposed at 39. @neo-gpt-emmy's review of PR #16774 falsified that census: the scanner could not see multiline method declarations or `const me = this` receiver aliases. Repairing those two blind spots surfaced 33 further obligations, including two files (ai/graph/storage/SQLite.mjs, ai/mcp/client/Client.mjs) that were entirely invisible. 39 was the instrument's reach, not the tree's population.
$schema.shrinkLane: Every entry here is a candidate for a discipline. The highest-value ones are truthy-skip entries on WRITE paths — see the purgeSession entries, where silence means a caller is told a purge succeeded that deleted nothing.
$schema.outOfScope: Members assigned outside initAsync(), and cross-file reads (ServiceA's member read by ServiceB). This lint is per-file by construction; see the header's bounds.

ai/Agent.mjs#ready:initError.reason: Deliberate. This IS the readiness machinery — it re-throws a stored construction error to the awaiting caller. A member whose whole purpose is to be absent on the happy path cannot carry an absence guard that throws.
ai/Agent.mjs#ready:initError.witness: ai/Agent.mjs — `ready()` tests `initError` and rethrows it; absence is the success case.

ai/Agent.mjs#schedule:loop.reason: Deliberate. `schedule()` guards `!this.loop` before touching the scheduler, so an event scheduled before the loop exists is dropped rather than crashing.

ai/Agent.mjs#start:loop.reason: Deliberate. `start()` on an un-initialised agent is a no-op by design.

EXAMINED, and accepted only because fixing it is out of scope here — the registry's highest-value shrink candidate. When the collection is absent the delete is skipped and the method still returns `{success: true, deletedMemories: 0}` with the message 'deleted 0 memories', which a caller cannot distinguish from a genuinely empty session. The WAL tombstone pass above it runs UNCONDITIONALLY, so the window produces a torn purge: tombstones written, content rows retained, success reported. Reachable because the MCP server's `prepareStartupDependency` catches a failed `SessionService.ready()` and keeps serving by design.
